canonical.:question/problem: Express $\cos\left( x - \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right)$ in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x.$
canonical.:question/worked-solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\cos(u - v) = \cos u \cos v + \sin u \sin v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u = x$ and $v = \dfrac{\pi}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(x-\frac{\pi }{2}\right) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right)+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡\left(\frac{\pi }{2}\right) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot 0+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot 1 \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
